key_insight: In Sr1-xNdxCoO3-δ perovskites, increasing oxygen content drives a vacancy-ordered structural transition from layered I4/mmm to orthorhombic Pmmm, along with a magnetic shift from weakly ferromagnetic G-type antiferromagnetism to ferromagnetism and a strong resistivity drop.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that oxygen stoichiometry and vacancy ordering can be used as practical levers to tune crystal structure, magnetism, and conductivity in cobalt-based perovskites for oxide electronics and related device materials.
method: Magnetic and electrotransport measurements versus oxygen content
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic diffraction and property measurements across x = 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3, linking oxygen uptake to structural, magnetic, and transport changes.
watch_item: The conductive ferromagnetic state is described as magnetically inhomogeneous due to residual oxygen vacancies, so performance may be sensitive to oxygen control and phase coexistence.
